title: Walderalm Alpine Pasture Gnadenwald & Karwendel
name: Walderalm Alpine Pasture Gnadenwald & Karwendel
kurzbeschreibung: Walderalm at 1,511 m on the Gnadenwald sunny plateau: traditional 17th-century alpine pasture with its own dairy, Guardian Angel Chapel, and Inntal views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The idyllic Walderalm is located on a sun-drenched plateau at an elevation of 1,511 metres above sea level on the southern foothills of the Karwendel Nature Park in the Tyrolean municipality of Gnadenwald (Bezirk Innsbruck-Land). Situated directly at the base of the mighty precipices of Vomper Loch and the Walderkamm ridge, the ensemble of three ancient timber and stone alpine huts is considered one of the most traditional and picturesque alpine pastures in the entire Inntal valley. With its sheltered panoramic location, the alpine meadow commands unmatched views overlooking the Inntal, the Tux foothills, and the distinctive Glungezer summit.

Alpine Culture, Dairy & Chapel

Documented records of Walderalm date back to the year 1344; the core structure of today's alpine buildings originates from the 17th century and has preserved its rustic, heritage-listed character unaltered. On the lush alpine meadows, around 70 dairy cows graze throughout the summer months, with their high-grade milk freshly processed every day in the on-site alpine cheese dairy. Visitors sitting on hand-carved wooden benches in front of the alpine huts can savour homemade Walder mountain cheese, fresh alpine butter, buttermilk, and hearty Tyrolean bacon platters. A particular gem is the picturesque Schutzengelkapelle (Guardian Angel Chapel) adjacent to the huts: built in 1968, this shingle-roofed small chapel provides a peaceful sanctuary for quiet reflection amidst high-alpine nature. The alpine pasture is also a crossroads of popular hiking and mountain bike trails leading to the neighbouring Hinterhornalm or up towards the Hundskopf peak.

Visit & Getting There

Walderalm is continuously catered daily without closing days during the alpine summer season from mid-May to late October (often remaining open until All Saints' Day in case of stable autumn weather). Arriving by car: from Hall in Tirol via Absam to Gnadenwald and up the toll-based Hinterhorn-Mautstraße toll road to the Hinterhornalm car park (1,522 m, toll approx. €5.00 per car). From there, a completely level, beautifully wide panoramic walking trail leads in just 25 to 30 minutes of gentle walking directly to Walderalm. Alternatively: a scenic mountain hike on foot starting from Gnadenwald/St. Martin (walking time approx. 1.5 hours). By public transport: regional bus from Innsbruck/Hall to the Gnadenwald St. Martin bus stop.

Tips

The panoramic trail from the Hinterhornalm car park to Walderalm is wide and gravelled, features virtually no elevation changes, and is ideally suited for families with strollers as well as seniors. Be sure to try the freshly fried Tyrolean Kiachln served with cranberries or sauerkraut, freshly prepared right outside the hut on sunny weekends.
